previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, hypertension, prior pulmonary embolism, and recent pneumonia was admitted for acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain concerning for ovarian torsion. Pelvic ultrasound showed normal ovaries with preserved blood flow, making torsion unlikely. Her pain resolved quickly with conservative management, and her exam normalized. Tachycardia persisting in the 110s–130s prompted a CT angiogram, which ruled out pulmonary embolism; the elevated heart rate was attributed to deconditioning and recent illness. An initial blood culture positive for coagulase-negative staph was deemed a contaminant, supported by a negative repeat culture and absence of infection signs. She completed a course of cefpodoxime for ongoing pneumonia treatment and was discharged home on hospital day two with plans for outpatient echocardiogram and physical therapy for joint pain and deconditioning.

HISTORY:  ___ female with leukocytosis.  Assess for pneumonia.

COMPARISONS:  ___ and CT, ___.

first rib corresponds to an area of osseous calcification, better appreciated
on the CT of ___.  The lung volumes are low, limiting exam sensitivity. 
Bibasilar atelectasis, left greater than right, is probably unchanged compared
to ___.  There are no focal areas of definite consolidation.  There are no
appreciable pleural effusions.  The cardiomediastinal contours are stable.

IMPRESSION:  Somewhat low lung volumes.  No focal consolidation.  Bibasilar
atelectasis, left greater than right, unchanged compared to ___.

STUDY:  Two views of each knee, ___.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with obesity.

FINDINGS:  There is a large amount of soft tissues which limits evaluation.
There is medial compartmental joint space narrowing bilaterally, left side
worse than right.  There are no signs for acute bony injury.  Evaluation for
joint effusion cannot be ascertained based on these images due to the large
amount of soft tissue.  No focal osseous lesions are seen.

INDICATION:  Patient is a ___ female with hypoxia and tachycardia. For
evaluation of pulmonary embolism.

EXAMINATION:  CTA of the chest with and without intravenous contrast.

COMPARISONS:  Comparison to CT chest examinations from ___ and CT torso
from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Hellically-acquired axial images were obtained from the mid chest
to the mid abdomen after the administration of 150 cc of Optiray intravenous
contrast using a CTA protocol.  The lung apices are excluded from the study.
There is a suboptimal contrast bolus timing with the bolus timing delayed from
an ideal pulmonary artery opacification phase.  In addition, there is poor
penetration which limits the study.  Coronal, sagittal, right and left oblique
images reformations were obtained.

FINDINGS:

Within the medial segmental branch of the right lower lobe pulmonary artery,
there is a low-attenuation filling defect that is centrally located with mild
expansion of the vessel.  This area is highly suspicious for a pulmonary
embolism involving the medial segmental branch of the right lower lobe. In the
left lower lobe, focal hypodensity in a left lower lobe pulmonary branch
(2:43) could be due to streak artifact as there is no definite expansion of
the vessel.  No other suspicious areas of intraluminal filling defects that
would be concerning for pulmonary embolism. The aorta and great vessels are
unremarkable, with no evidence of aortic dissection. The heart is normal in
appearance.  There is persistent diffuse ground-glass opacity seen within the
imaged portions of the lungs that demonstrates interval improvement since
examination from ___ with bilateral linear atelectasis and an area of more
focal density involving the left lower lobe that is linear in configuration,
not significantly changed from ___ that could represent a focal area of
atelectasis.  The imaged portions of the lungs are otherwise clear with no new
focal parenchymal opacities or pleural effusions. No pulmonary nodules are
identified.  There are multiple scattered lymph nodes throughout the
mediastinum and bilateral axilla that do not meet size criteria for pathologic
enlargement.

The imaged portions of liver and spleen appear unremarkable.

BONE WINDOWS:  The visualized osseous structures are unremarkable with no
suspicious lytic or sclerotic foci identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Centrally located pulmonary arterial intraluminal filling defect seen
within the medial segment of the right lower lobe highly suspicious for a
right lower lobe pulmonary embolism despite limitations of the study.
Questionable filling defect in left lower lobe pulmonary artery could be
artifactual.

2.  Slight interval improvement in diffuse ground-glass opacities as seen on
most recent chest CT from ___, with bilateral atelectasis.

These findings were discussed with Dr. ___ at 7:30 p.m. on ___.

HISTORY:  Hypoxia.

COMPARISON:  U/S from ___.

FINDINGS:  The waveforms in the common femoral veins are symmetric bilaterally
with appropriate response to Valsalva maneuvers.  The common femoral veins,
proximal greater saphenous veins, superficial femoral veins and popliteal
veins are normal bilaterally with appropriate compression, wall-to-wall flow
on color analysis as well as appropriate response to waveform and
augmentation.  The posterior tibial and peroneal veins in the calves
bilaterally are not well visualized.  Posterior to the right knee is an
anechoic structure measuring 29 x 10 x 45 mm, and in keeping with a ___
cyst, decreased in size since ___.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of DVT and redemonstration of a right posterior
popliteal fluid collection likely a ___ cyst.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
